The ruling is general: each person, man or woman, will have a share of what he or she earns by his or her own effort, so do not envy the other, and ask Allah for His bounty, for He gives whom He wills, and Allah is All-Knowing of all things, knowing who deserves what.

phrases.ar: وَلِكُلّٖ جَعَلۡنَا مَوَٰلِيَ مِمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَانِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبُونَۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ عَقَدَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ فَـَٔاتُوهُمۡ نَصِيبَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ شَهِيدًا
phrases.translation: And We have appointed heirs to what has been left by parents and next of kin. As for those you have made a pledge to, give them their share. Surely Allah is a Witness over all things
phrases.explanation: "And We have appointed heirs to what has been left by parents and next of kin. And those to whom your right hands have made a covenant, give them their share. Allah is indeed Witness over all things." Allah says that for everyone He has appointed heirs, the mawali, to what is left by the parents and the next of kin, and this is the inheritance. And for those to whom your right hands have made a covenant, the old oath of brotherhood in the pre-Islamic era by which they used to inherit one another, give them their share, for the covenant was binding. And Allah is Witness over all things, seeing who gives the rights and who withholds them, and He will requite everyone according to his deed. The mawali are called so because the Arabs called the son of the paternal uncle a mawlā, an heir who inherits, and the poets used the word for the cousin who is strove for. And the covenant of the right hands is the oath of brotherhood that was made in the pre-Islamic era, by which two men became heirs to one another, and Allah has commanded to give them their share from the inheritance, and this was before it was abrogated. And Allah is Witness over all things, and He knows who fulfilled the covenant and who broke it, and He will judge between them on the Day of Judgment. And He is Witness.

phrases.ar: ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٰمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٖ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡۚ فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ قَٰنِتَٰتٌ حَٰفِظَٰتٞ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ
phrases.translation: Men are the caretakers of women, as men have been provisioned by Allah over women and tasked with supporting them financially. And righteous women are devoutly obedient and, when alone, protective of what Allah has entrusted them with. And if you
phrases.explanation: "Men are the caretakers of women, as men have been provisioned by Allah over women and because of what they spend of their wealth. So the righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding the unseen as Allah has guarded. And those from whom you fear rebellion, admonish them, forsake them in beds, and discipline them. But if they obey you, seek not a way against them. Allah is indeed Ever-High, Great." Allah says men are the maintainers and caretakers of women, because He has favored some of them over others in strength and provision, and because they spend of their wealth on them. The righteous women are devoutly obedient to Allah and to their husbands, guarding in the unseen what Allah has guarded, preserving themselves and their husbands' honor. And as for those women from whom you fear rebellion and disobedience, admonish them first, then forsake them in the beds, then discipline them, and the exegetes differed over the manner of the discipline. But if they obey you after that, do not seek a way against them, and forgive. And Allah is Ever-High above all, Great in His attributes, and He sees what you do. It was said this was revealed concerning a man who struck his wife, and the scholars discussed whether there is retaliation between spouses for less than life. And because of what they spend of their wealth, meaning the men spend on the women from their wealth, and that is why they are the maintainers. And the righteous women are devoutly obedient, obedient to Allah and to their husbands.

phrases.ar: بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱلَّٰتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّۖ فَإِنۡ أَطَعۡنَكُمۡ فَلَا تَبۡغُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ سَبِيلًاۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيّٗا كَبِيرٗا
phrases.translation: sense ill-conduct from your women, advise them ˹first˺, ˹if they persist,˺ do not share their beds, ˹but if they still persist,˺ then discipline them ˹gently˺. But if they change their ways, do not be unjust to them. Surely Allah is Most High, All-Great
phrases.explanation: "But if they obey you, seek not a way against them. Allah is indeed Ever-High, Great." If the wife returns to obedience after the admonition and separation, then do not seek a way against her and do not harm her, for Allah is Ever-High, Ever-Great, and He has commanded forbearance, and He sees the hearts and the dealings, and He will judge between the spouses. The exegetes discussed the steps against the rebellious wife: admonition with words, then separation in the beds, then discipline, and they differed over the manner of the discipline, some saying a strike that does not wound, and others that it is limited. And if she obeys after that, do not seek a way against her, and Allah is Ever-High, Great in His attributes and His judgment, and He sees the obedience and the rebellion, and He will requite each spouse according to her deed, and He does not wrong anyone. And the exegetes said the obedient women guard themselves in the absence of their husbands, preserving their chastity and their husbands' wealth, as Allah has commanded, and the reciters differed over the reading of that phrase. And whoever does this is among the righteous, and Allah loves the righteous, and He is Ever-High, Great, and He does not wrong anyone, and He will admit the obedient into Paradise. And if she disobeys again, the steps are repeated, and the goal is her return to obedience, and Allah sees all, and He is Ever-High, Great, and He judges with justice between the spouses. And the wisdom in the gradual steps is to give the wife a chance to return at each stage, and the exegetes said the discipline is a strike that does not break a bone, and some said it is symbolic, but all agree that harming her grievously is forbidden, and the goal is reform, not revenge. And Allah is Ever-High, Great, and He sees whether the husband is just or oppressive, and He will hold him to account.

phrases.ar: وَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ شِقَاقَ بَيۡنِهِمَا فَٱبۡعَثُواْ حَكَمٗا مِّنۡ أَهۡلِهِۦ وَحَكَمٗا مِّنۡ أَهۡلِهَآ إِن يُرِيدَآ إِصۡلَٰحٗا يُوَفِّقِ ٱللَّهُ بَيۡنَهُمَآۗ
phrases.translation: If you anticipate a split between them, appoint a mediator from his family and another from hers. If they desire reconciliation, Allah will restore harmony
phrases.explanation: "If you anticipate a split between them, appoint a mediator from his family and a mediator from her family. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will unite them. Allah is indeed All-Knowing, All-Aware." Allah commands that if you fear a split between the spouses, send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family, and if both sides desire reconciliation, Allah will unite them and remove the discord. The exegetes discussed the two arbiters and said they are to judge between them and reconcile if possible. And Allah is All-Knowing of the hearts, All-Aware of what is hidden, and He knows whether the reconciliation is sincere, and He will reward the peacemakers. Shiqaq is the dispute when each of the two sides hardens against the other. The exegetes differed over who is commanded to send the arbiters: some said it is the ruler before whom the matter is brought, others the husband and the wife themselves. And they differed over what the two arbiters may do, whether they may reconcile or also separate with compensation. In all views, if both desire reconciliation, Allah will unite them, and He is All-Knowing of the hearts, All-Aware of the hidden, and He knows the sincerity of each side, and He rewards the peacemakers and removes the discord. Some said the two spouses send them with authorization to investigate their case, and it is not permissible for the arbiters to separate them except with the consent of both, and others said the ruler sends them only to ascertain the situation and reconcile. And the arbiters should be just, from the family of each side, and if they judge that separation is better, they may do so with a fair compensation, but if both desire reconciliation, Allah will unite them. And the verse enjoins justice and kindness between the spouses, for the family is the foundation of society, and Allah is All-Knowing of what is hidden in the hearts, All-Aware of the plots, and He knows who is the oppressor and who is the oppressed. And the best of affairs is reconciliation. And the arbiters should be from the family of each side so that they know the situation and can speak frankly, and they should be righteous and just, and if they find that the husband is the oppressor, they restrain him, and if the wife is the rebel, they admonish her. And if they cannot reconcile them, they may separate them with a fair settlement. And Allah is All-Knowing of what is hidden, All-Aware of the hearts, and He knows who desires reconciliation sincerely, and He will unite them.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا خَبِيرٗا
phrases.translation: between them. Surely Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware
phrases.explanation: "If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will unite them. Allah is indeed All-Knowing, All-Aware." If both desire reconciliation and the arbiters work for it, Allah will unite their hearts and remove the enmity, for He is All-Knowing, All-Aware of what is in the hearts. And the reconciliation is a good deed, and Allah loves those who reconcile between people, and He will unite their hearts if they are sincere. And whoever reconciles between people, Allah loves him. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware. And whoever does this for Allah, He will reward him. And He will unite them with His permission. And He is All-Aware of the hidden.

phrases.ar: ۞ وَٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـٔٗاۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنٗا وَبِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱلۡجَارِ ذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡجَارِ ٱلۡجُنُبِ وَٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلۡجَنۢبِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
phrases.translation: Worship Allah ˹alone˺ and associate none with Him. And be kind to parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, near and distant neighbours, close friends, ˹needy˺ travellers, and those
phrases.explanation: "Worship Allah alone and associate none with Him. And be kind to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the distant neighbor, the companion at your side, the wayfarer, and those in your possession. Allah does not love the arrogant, boastful ones." Allah commands worship of Him alone with no partners, and kindness to the parents, the relatives, the orphans, the needy, the near and the distant neighbor, the companion at your side, the traveler, and the slaves in your possession. And He forbids arrogance and boasting, for Allah does not love the arrogant one who boasts, and He knows what is in the hearts, and He will requite the kind and the arrogant. Kindness to parents means obedience to them and speaking to them kindly, and to the kinsmen means maintaining the ties, and to the orphans means the child whose father has died, be compassionate to him, and to the needy, the one overcome by poverty, and to the near neighbor who is also a kinsman, and the exegetes differed whether that means the neighbor of your kinsman or the kinsman who is your neighbor, or the neighbor bound to you by Islam, and to the far neighbor, the companion at your side, the wayfarer, and those your right hands possess, the slaves, be kind to them and treat them well. And Allah does not love the arrogant, boastful ones, and He knows what you hide, and He will requite you. The distant neighbor is the one far from you in dwelling, and the exegetes differed whether he is the neighbor in another place or the polytheist neighbor, but the meaning is general: be kind to every neighbor. And the companion at your side is the one who sits with you and the wayfarer is the traveler, and those your right hands possess are the servants and slaves, so be kind to them, feed them and clothe them and speak to them kindly. And do not be arrogant with your kindness, for Allah does not love the arrogant, and He is All-Knowing of what you do in secret and in public, and He will requite the doer of good with good and the arrogant with humiliation. And He is All-Forgiving to those who repent of arrogance. And the best of kindness is to the parents, for they raised you when you were small, so be dutiful to them in their old age. And the rights of the neighbor are many, so do not harm him, and the rights of the orphan and the needy are to be compassionate and generous, and Allah sees the kindness and He will reward it in this life and the next.

phrases.ar: وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخۡتَالٗا فَخُورًا
phrases.translation: ˹bondspeople˺ in your possession. Surely Allah does not like whoever is arrogant, boastful—
phrases.explanation: "Allah does not love the arrogant, boastful ones." He does not love whoever is arrogant and boasts over the people, and He knows the hidden, and He will punish the arrogant. And the arrogant one will be humiliated, and the kind one will be honored, for Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware, and He sees the secret and the open, and He does not wrong anyone. And the boastful one will be brought low, for Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware, and He does not love the arrogant, and He will punish him for his arrogance, and reward the humble kind doer. And He knows the hearts. And He is All-Just.

phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡخَلُونَ وَيَأۡمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلۡبُخۡلِ وَيَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
phrases.translation: those who are stingy, promote stinginess among people, and withhold Allah’s bounties. We have prepared for the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: "Those who are stingy, promote stinginess among people, and withhold Allah's bounties, then let them rejoice not in what they withhold. We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment." Allah describes the stingy ones who withhold what Allah has given them and order others to be stingy and hide the bounty of Allah from the people, promising them rejoicing in what they withheld, but their end is the humiliating punishment prepared for the disbelievers. The verse warns against miserliness and enjoins spending in the way of Allah, for the wealth is a trust, and the stingy one will regret it on the Day of Judgment, when his wealth will not avail him. And the grammar of the verse shows the stingy are condemned, and the bounty withheld is from Allah, so it is not theirs to withhold. And whoever spends in the way of Allah, Allah will replace it for him, and whoever is stingy, Allah will make him poor in his heart, and his wealth will go to others after him, and he will carry the sin of withholding.

phrases.ar: عَذَابٗا مُّهِينٗا
phrases.translation: a humiliating punishment
phrases.explanation: "We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment." The punishment is humiliating because it is everlasting, and the stingy disbeliever will abide in it. And it will be said to him on the Day of Judgment: this is the punishment you prepared for yourself by your disbelief and your stinginess, and nothing of your wealth will avail you then, for Allah is All-Just and He does not wrong anyone, and the humiliating punishment is everlasting for the disbelievers. And the disbelievers will abide in it forever. And Allah is severe in punishment. And no one will be wronged, for the punishment is for the disbelief and the withholding of rights, and Allah has made the punishment clear in His Book.

phrases.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَلَا بِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۗ
phrases.translation: Likewise for those who spend their wealth to show off and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day. And
phrases.explanation: "Likewise for those who spend their wealth to show off and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day. Whoever has Satan as a companion, what an evil companion he is!" Allah says the same applies to those who spend their wealth for show, to be seen by people, and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day: their spending is not accepted, for it is done for other than Allah. And whoever has Satan as a companion, what an evil companion he is, for Satan orders evil and forbids good, and leads his companion to the Fire. And show is a disease of the heart.

phrases.ar: وَمَن يَكُنِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لَهُۥ قَرِينٗا فَسَآءَ قَرِينٗا
phrases.translation: whoever takes Satan as an associate—what an evil associate they have
phrases.explanation: "What harm could have come to them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent out of what Allah has provided them? Allah is All-Knowing of you." If they had believed and spent for Allah, no harm would have come to them, and they would have been rewarded. But they chose show and disbelief, and Allah is All-Knowing of you, knowing the intentions, and He will requite the sincere and the show-off. And the sincere spending is accepted and multiplied, while the show-off spending is rejected, for Allah is All-Knowing of the hearts and He knows who spends for Him and who spends for the people.

phrases.ar: وَمَاذَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ لَوۡ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَأَنفَقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِمۡ عَلِيمًا
phrases.translation: What harm could have come to them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and donated from what Allah has provided for them? And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of them
phrases.explanation: "What harm could have come to them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent out of what Allah has provided them? Allah is All-Knowing of you." Allah says: what harm could come to them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent of what Allah provided them for His sake. The answer is: no harm, rather good and reward, for the believer who spends sincerely will be recompensed, while the one who spends for show will get nothing. And Allah is All-Knowing of you, knowing your intentions and your deeds, and He will judge between the sincere and the hypocrite on the Day of Judgment. And He knows all.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظۡلِمُ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٖۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةٗ
phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah never wrongs ˹anyone˺—even by an atom’s weight. And if it is a good deed, He will multiply it many
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, Allah never wrongs anyone, even by an atom's weight. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward." Allah says He does not wrong anyone even by the weight of an atom, and if the deed is good, He multiplies it many times and grants from Himself a great reward. So the believer need not fear that his good deed will be lost, for Allah records it and multiplies it, and the wrong is also recorded but Allah forgives much. And the exegetes discussed the atom's weight and said it means the smallest thing, and that the good is multiplied tenfold to seven hundredfold and more. And the wrong, even by an atom, will be requited, but Allah forgives much of it by His mercy.

phrases.ar: يُضَٰعِفۡهَا وَيُؤۡتِ مِن لَّدُنۡهُ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمٗا
phrases.translation: times over and will give a great reward out of His grace
phrases.explanation: "He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward." The reward is multiplied beyond measure, and the great reward is Paradise, which Allah grants from His bounty to whom He wills. And the great reward is from the bounty of Allah, and He gives it to the believers who do good, and He is All-Generous, and He does not wrong anyone, and the exegetes said the multiplication has no limit, and Allah increases whom He wills. And whoever hopes for it, let him do good. And He is All-Bountiful. And the exegetes differed over the limit of the multiplication, some saying it is up to seven hundredfold, others more, but all agree Allah multiplies the reward of the good deed and He is All-Generous, Most Merciful.

phrases.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جِئۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةِۭ بِشَهِيدٖ وَجِئۡنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ شَهِيدٗا
phrases.translation: So how will it be when We bring a witness from every faith-community and bring you ˹O Prophet˺ as a witness against yours
phrases.explanation: "So how will it be when We bring a witness from every faith-community and bring you as a witness over these people?" Allah asks how it will be on the Day of Judgment, when He brings from every community a witness, its prophet, to testify for or against it, and brings you, O Muhammad, as a witness over these people, your community. The exegetes said the witness from every nation testifies to what his nation did, and you testify to what your nation did, and Allah judges between all with justice, and no one will be wronged, for He is the best of judges. And He is All-Just.

phrases.ar: يَوۡمَئِذٖ يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَعَصَوُاْ ٱلرَّسُولَ
phrases.translation: On that Day, those who denied ˹Allah˺ and disobeyed the Messenger will wish they were
phrases.explanation: "On that Day, those who denied Allah and disobeyed the Messenger will wish the ground would be leveled with them. And they will hide nothing from Allah." On the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers who disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them, out of regret for their disbelief, but it will not be, and they will hide nothing from Allah, for He knows all that they conceal and reveal. And the earth will not be leveled over them, for the punishment is greater, and they will be in the Fire, and they will wish they had obeyed, but it will not avail them.

phrases.ar: لَوۡ تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَلَا يَكۡتُمُونَ ٱللَّهَ حَدِيثٗا
phrases.translation: reduced to dust. And they will never be able to hide anything from Allah
phrases.explanation: "And they will hide nothing from Allah." Everything they did will be shown to them, and they will confess it, for Allah has recorded it and He is All-Knowing, and no secret is hidden from Him, and they will wish they had never disobeyed, but regret will not avail them then. And nothing is hidden from Allah, neither a secret nor a whisper, and He has recorded every deed in the Book, and He will show it to them on that Day, and they will be ashamed and regretful, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware. And they will be held to account. And He is the best of judges.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَنتُمۡ سُكَٰرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعۡلَمُواْ مَا تَقُولُونَ وَلَا جُنُبًا إِلَّا عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتَّىٰ تَغۡتَسِلُواْۚ وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرۡضَىٰٓ أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ أَحَدٞ مِّنكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡغَآئِطِ أَوۡ لَٰمَسۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَلَمۡ تَجِدُواْ مَآءٗ فَتَيَمَّمُواْ
phrases.translation: O believers! Do not approach prayer while intoxicated until you are aware of what you say, nor in a state of ˹full˺ impurity—unless you merely pass through ˹the mosque˺—until you have bathed. But if you are ill, on a journey, or have relieved yourselves, or been intimate with your wives and cannot find water, then purify
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Do not approach prayer while intoxicated until you are aware of what you say, nor in a state of ritual impurity until you have washed, except when passing through. If you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you has just relieved himself, or you have had contact with women, and you cannot find water, then wipe your faces and hands with clean earth. Allah is indeed Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving." Allah forbids the believers from approaching prayer while drunk, until they know what they say, and while in ritual impurity until they wash, except one passing through the mosque. And if they are ill, traveling, have relieved themselves, or have had contact with women, and find no water, they may wipe their faces and hands with clean earth, the tayammum. The exegetes differed over the meaning of passing through and over the ruling for the traveler, but all agree that Allah has made the religion easy and permitted the tayammum out of mercy, and Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving to His servants, so He forgives the one who errs and accepts the one who repents. The exegetes differed over the intoxication meant: some said it is the intoxication of wine, and others said it is also the intoxication of sleep, so that the one who is sleepy should wait until he is awake. And they differed over the recitation of the verse and over how the drunk person can know what he says when his reason has gone, and the answer is that he should not approach prayer until he is sober and aware. And the tayammum with clean earth is a concession from Allah for the one who cannot use water, and the exegetes discussed its manner, wiping the face and the hands, and said it replaces the washing when water is unavailable or harmful. And Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving, so He pardons the one who forgets and the one who errs, and He accepts the tayammum as a purification, and He knows the situations of His servants, so He legislated it out of mercy and ease. And the reason for the prohibition of prayer while drunk is that the prayer requires presence of heart and clear speech, and the drunk person cannot do that, so Allah forbade it until he is aware. And the state of ritual impurity requires the full washing, except the traveler passing through the mosque, for he does not stay. And the concessions for illness, travel, and the absence of water are all from the mercy of Allah, and He has made the religion easy, and He is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving, and He loves that His servants take His concessions, for He is All-Generous. And He knows your situations.

phrases.ar: صَعِيدٗا طَيِّبٗا فَٱمۡسَحُواْ بِوُجُوهِكُمۡ وَأَيۡدِيكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا
phrases.translation: yourselves with clean earth, wiping your faces and hands. And Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving
phrases.explanation: "Allah is indeed Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving." He pardons the sin and forgives the one who does the tayammum in the permitted case, and He forgives much, and He knows the situations of His servants, so He permitted the earth when water is not found. And whoever does the tayammum with a valid excuse, his prayer is valid, and Allah is All-Forgiving of the past, Most Merciful to His servants, and He does not burden a soul beyond its capacity, and He knows what is best for you, and He guides whom He wills. And the concession is a mercy. And He is All-Generous, and He does not burden you.

phrases.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ نَصِيبٗا مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ
phrases.translation: Have you ˹O Prophet˺ not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures yet
phrases.explanation: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who are invited to the Scripture of Allah to judge between them, but some of them turn away, for they do not want to judge by it." Allah addresses the Prophet: have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, the Jews, who are called to the Book of Allah to judge between them, but a party of them turns away, because they do not want to judge by what Allah revealed. The exegetes differed over who is meant and over the turning away, but the meaning is that they were invited to the truth and refused it, and that is a sign of their disbelief.

phrases.ar: يَشۡتَرُونَ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَن تَضِلُّواْ ٱلسَّبِيلَ
phrases.translation: trade it for misguidance and wish to see you deviate from the ˹Right˺ Path
phrases.explanation: "But some of them turn away, for they do not want to judge by it." They turn away from the judgment of Allah because their desires oppose it, and whoever turns away from the truth after knowing it is astray, and Allah knows the wrongdoers. And the exegetes said the turning away is from the judgment of the Book of Allah, for they prefer the judgment of their desires, and that is the mark of the disbeliever, and Allah knows the wrongdoers, and He will requite them for their turning away from the truth, and He is All-Knowing of what they conceal. And He requites them. And He sees it.

phrases.ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِأَعۡدَآئِكُمۡۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَلِيّٗا وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ نَصِيرٗا
phrases.translation: Allah knows best who your enemies are! And Allah is sufficient as a Guardian, and He is sufficient as a Helper
phrases.explanation: "Allah knows best who your enemies are! And Allah is sufficient as a Guardian, and Allah is sufficient as a Helper." Allah says He knows best the enemies of the believers, those who harbor enmity, and He informed them of the enmity of those whom He forbade, so beware of them. And Allah is sufficient as a Guardian for the believers, protecting them, and sufficient as a Helper, aiding them against their enemies. So rely on Allah and do not fear the enemies, for He is All-Knowing of them and All-Powerful over them. And He knows their plots and their enmity. And do not fear them. And He is All-Powerful.

phrases.ar: مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ غَيۡرَ مُسۡمَعٖ وَرَٰعِنَا لَيَّۢا بِأَلۡسِنَتِهِمۡ وَطَعۡنٗا فِي ٱلدِّينِۚ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَأَطَعۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ وَٱنظُرۡنَا لَكَانَ خَيۡرٗا لَّهُمۡ وَأَقۡوَمَ
phrases.translation: Some Jews take words out of context and say, “We listen and we disobey,” “Hear! May you never hear,” and “Râ’ina!” [Herd us!]—playing with words and discrediting the faith. Had they said ˹courteously˺, “We hear and obey,” “Listen to us,” and “Unẓurna,” [Tend to us!] it would have been better for them and more proper. Allah
phrases.explanation: "Some Jews take words out of context and say, We listen and we disobey, Hear, may you not hear, and Rāina, twisting their tongues and slandering the religion. Had they said, We hear and we obey, and Listen, and Unẓurnā, it would have been better for them and more upright. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a few." Allah describes some of the Jews who distort the words from their places, twisting their tongues to mock the Muslims, saying words that sound like obedience but mean disobedience and mockery, such as their saying we hear and we disobey, and their addressing the Prophet with words that slander the religion. And Allah says had they said we hear and we obey, and listen, and look at us, it would have been better for them and more upright. But He has cursed them for their disbelief, so few of them believe. The verse warns the believers against the distortion of the enemies and enjoins them to speak clearly and believe. The exegetes differed over the meaning: some said the verse refers to all of those who were given a portion of the Book, others that it refers to some of the Jews who distort the words from their proper places, changing the meanings of the Scripture. And the words they twist are their sayings that carry mockery, and their addressing with words that slander the religion. And the verse shows that the distortion is a sign of disbelief, and the curse of Allah has befallen them, so they believe only a few, for Allah curses whom He wills and He is All-Just, and He guides whom He wills. And the believers should beware of the distortion of the enemies and hold fast to the clear Book, for the Book of Allah is preserved and the distortion of the disbelievers does not affect it, and Allah is the Guardian of His Book, and He knows the distorters, and He will requite them.

phrases.ar: وَلَٰكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡ فَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلٗا
phrases.translation: has condemned them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except for a few
phrases.explanation: "But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a few." The curse is because of their disbelief and their distortion, and few of them believe, for Allah guides whom He wills and He knows the wrongdoers. And the few who believe among them are those whom Allah guided, and He knows the believers, and He will reward them for their belief, and He is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers, and He will punish the disbelievers who distorted the words. And He is All-Just. And whoever believes, He will reward him, and whoever disbelieves, He will punish him, for He is All-Knowing of the hearts and He does not wrong anyone, and the disbelievers have gone astray by their distortion of the words.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ ءَامِنُواْ بِمَا نَزَّلۡنَا مُصَدِّقٗا لِّمَا مَعَكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن نَّطۡمِسَ وُجُوهٗا فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَدۡبَارِهَآ أَوۡ نَلۡعَنَهُمۡ
phrases.translation: O you who were given the Book! Believe in what We have revealed—confirming your own Scriptures—before We wipe out ˹your˺ faces, turning them backwards, or We
phrases.explanation: "O you who were given the Book! Believe in what We have revealed, confirming what you have, before We obliterate faces and turn them on their backs, or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath. And the command of Allah is ever fulfilled." Allah commands the People of the Book to believe in what He revealed to the Prophet, confirming the Scripture they have, before He punishes them by obliterating their faces and turning them backward, or cursing them. And the command of Allah is ever fulfilled, for when He wills something, it happens. The exegetes discussed the obliteration of faces and the curse, and said it is a severe punishment for disobedience, and they differed over whether it happened or is a threat. And the exegetes differed over the effacing of the faces: some said it means wiping away their features so they become like the backs of animals, others that it means blinding their eyes, and others that it is a threat and a warning. In all views, the punishment is severe, and the command of Allah is ever fulfilled, for He does what He wills, and He is All-Powerful over His servants.

phrases.ar: كَمَا لَعَنَّآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلسَّبۡتِۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولًا
phrases.translation: condemn the defiant as We did to the Sabbath-breakers. And Allah’s command is always executed
phrases.explanation: "Or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath. And the command of Allah is ever fulfilled." The curse is like the curse of the Sabbath people, and the command of Allah is executed, so hasten to belief before the punishment comes, and Allah is All-Powerful over all things. The people of the Sabbath were cursed because they transgressed the Sabbath, and their curse is mentioned in the Scripture, so this is a like punishment for the one who disobeys after being warned. And the command of Allah is executed, and no one can avert it, so hasten to obey before the punishment comes. And the exegetes said the verse is a warning to the People of the Book to believe in the Prophet before the punishment descends, for Allah does what He wills, and He is All-Powerful, and His command is ever fulfilled, and He knows what is best for His servants, so obey Him and believe. And fear Allah and return to Him. And the warning is clear, and the punishment is severe, and Allah does what He wills, and His command is ever fulfilled, so believe before it is too late, and Allah is All-Powerful, All-Wise, and He knows what is best for His servants, and He will judge between all with justice on the Day of Judgment.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ
phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating others with Him ˹in worship˺, but forgives anything else of
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating others with Him in worship, but forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has indeed gone far astray." Allah says He does not forgive shirk, associating partners with Him, for it is the greatest sin, but He forgives sins other than that for whom He wills, out of His mercy. And whoever commits shirk has gone far astray from the truth, for shirk is the greatest wrong. The exegetes discussed the grammar and said the verse means He does not forgive shirk for the one who dies upon it, and He forgives the lesser sins for whom He wills, whether by repentance or by His mercy.

phrases.ar: وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰٓ إِثۡمًا عَظِيمًا
phrases.translation: whoever He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has indeed committed a grave sin
phrases.explanation: "And whoever associates others with Allah has indeed gone far astray." He has gone astray from the straight path, and there is no sin greater than shirk, and whoever dies upon it will abide in the Fire forever, for Allah does not forgive it, and He is All-Just, and He has made the warning clear in His Book. And the exegetes said whoever repents from shirk before death, Allah may forgive him by His mercy, but whoever dies upon shirk, no forgiveness is for him, and he has gone far astray, and Allah is All-Knowing of who repents sincerely, and He accepts the repentance of His servants.

phrases.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُمۚ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَآءُ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
phrases.translation: Have you ˹O Prophet˺ not seen those who ˹falsely˺ elevate themselves? It is Allah who elevates whoever He wills. And none will be wronged ˹even by the width of˺ the thread
phrases.explanation: "Have you not seen those who falsely elevate themselves? It is Allah who elevates whom He wills. They were given a portion of the Scripture, but they disbelieved in falsehood. They did not wrong Us, but they wronged themselves." Allah asks the Prophet whether he has seen those who praise themselves and claim purity, but it is Allah who purifies whom He wills, not self-praise. And they were given a portion of the Scripture but disbelieved in falsehood, the jibt and the taghut, false objects of worship. And they did not wrong Allah, for Allah does not need their belief, but they wronged themselves by their disbelief, and they will be punished for it. The exegetes differed over what their declaring themselves pure was: some said it was their claim that they are the children of Allah and His beloved, others that they praised themselves before the Prophet and claimed they were purer than the believers. In all views, self-praise is blameworthy, for purity is from Allah, and He purifies whom He wills by faith and good deeds. And they were given a portion of the Scripture, the Torah, but they disbelieved in the falsehood they were warned against, and their disbelief wrongs only themselves, for Allah is All-Just and needs nothing from His servants, and He will judge between all on the Day of Judgment. And the verse is a refutation of self-praise and a proof that guidance and purity are from Allah alone, so do not praise yourself, and ask Allah to purify you, for He is All-Knowing of who is pure. And He does not wrong.

phrases.ar: فَتِيلًا
phrases.translation: of a date stone
phrases.explanation: "They did not wrong Us, but they wronged themselves." The wrong falls on the doer, and Allah is All-Just, and He does not wrong anyone. And whoever wrongs himself, Allah does not wrong him, and the punishment is for the wrongdoer, and Allah is All-Knowing of the hearts, and He will requite the self-praiser and the wrongdoer, for He does not wrong anyone, and He is the best of judges. And Allah is All-Powerful over all things. And whoever disbelieves, his disbelief harms only himself, and Allah is All-Knowing of the doers, and He will judge between them on the Day of Judgment, and He is the best of judges, and He does not wrong anyone in an atom's weight.

phrases.ar: ٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ يَفۡتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَۖ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِۦٓ إِثۡمٗا مُّبِينًا
phrases.translation: See how they fabricate lies against Allah—this alone is a blatant sin
phrases.explanation: "See how they fabricate lies against Allah, this alone is a blatant sin." Allah says: look at how those who claim knowledge fabricate lies against Allah, attributing to Him what is not true, and that alone, without anything else, is a blatant, clear sin. And the exegetes discussed the fabrication and said it is their claim that the Quran is fabricated, and that is a great sin, for whoever lies against Allah has gone astray, and Allah is All-Knowing of the liars, and He will requite them. And the lie against Allah is the greatest of lies, and whoever fabricates against Allah, Allah is All-Knowing of him, and He will requite him with a painful punishment, for lying against Allah is a blatant sin that leads to the Fire.

phrases.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ نَصِيبٗا مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡجِبۡتِ وَٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ أَهۡدَىٰ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ سَبِيلًا
phrases.translation: Have you ˹O Prophet˺ not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures yet believe in idols and false gods and reassure the disbelievers that they are better guided than the believers
phrases.explanation: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture believing in falsehood and false gods, and saying of the disbelievers, These are better guided than the believers?" Allah asks whether the Prophet has seen those given a portion of the Book who believe in jibt and taghut, falsehood and false gods, and who say of the disbelievers that they are better guided than the believers. That is a great error, for the believers are the ones upon guidance, and the disbelievers are upon error. The exegetes said they preferred the disbelievers because the disbelievers were rich and numerous, while the believers were few, and that shows their love of this world over the Hereafter, and Allah knows the astray. The exegetes differed over the jibt and the taghut: some said they are two idols the polytheists worshipped besides Allah, others that the jibt are the idols and the taghut are their spokesmen, and others that jibt is everything worshipped besides Allah and taghut is Satan. In all views, believing in them is disbelief, and their saying that the disbelievers are better guided than the believers is a great error. And the reason they said that was that the disbelievers were numerous and wealthy while the believers were few, and that shows their love of the world, and Allah knows the astray, and He will judge between the believers and the disbelievers with justice, and the believers are upon the truth, and He is All-Knowing of who is guided. Others said the jibt is the soothsayer and the taghut is a man of the Jews, others that the jibt is sorcery and the taghut is Satan, and others that the jibt is the sorcerer and the taghut is the devil. And in all the views, they are false things that were worshipped besides Allah, and believing in them is disbelief. And those who said the disbelievers are better guided were wrong, for guidance is with the believers, and Allah knows who is upon guidance and who is astray, and He will requite each according to his deed, and the believers will be in Paradise, and He is All-Knowing, All-Just. And the believers are better guided, and Allah knows the believers. And He will reward them.

phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ وَمَن يَلۡعَنِ ٱللَّهُ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُۥ نَصِيرًا
phrases.translation: It is they who have been condemned by Allah. And whoever is condemned by Allah will have no helper
phrases.explanation: "It is they who have been condemned by Allah. And whoever is condemned by Allah, you will never find for him a helper." Allah says those are the ones whom He has cursed, and whoever Allah curses, no one can help him or avert the punishment from him, for the curse of Allah is executed. And the exegetes discussed the curse and said it means He has removed His mercy from them, and they are in the Fire, and no helper will aid them, and Allah is All-Powerful over His servants. And the helper is the one who aids and protects, and there is none for the cursed one, for Allah is All-Powerful, and His curse is a removal of His mercy, and they will abide in the Fire, and no one will help them, and Allah does what He wills, and He is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers.

phrases.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ نَصِيبٞ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُلۡكِ فَإِذٗا لَّا يُؤۡتُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ نَقِيرًا
phrases.translation: Do they have control over shares of the kingdom? If so, they would not have given anyone so much as the speck on a date stone
phrases.explanation: "Do they have control over shares of the kingdom? If so, they would not have given people a speck on a date pit. Or do they envy the people for Allah's bounties? Indeed, We have given the Scripture to the family of Abraham and given them the kingdom, and We have given them a great kingdom." Allah refutes the claim of some that they have a share of the kingdom or power: if they had, they would not give anyone even a speck on a date pit, for the stingy withhold. And He says they envy the people for the bounty Allah has given them, the prophethood and the Book. But indeed Allah gave the Book and the kingdom to the family of Abraham, and gave them a great kingdom, so the envy is unjustified, for the bounty is from Allah and He gives it to whom He wills. The exegetes differed over the meaning, but the preferred view is that the verse refutes the claim of ownership and affirms that the bounty is from Allah.

phrases.ar: أَمۡ يَحۡسُدُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَىٰ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۖ
phrases.translation: Or do they envy the people for Allah’s bounties? Indeed, We have given
phrases.explanation: "Or do they envy the people for Allah's bounties? Indeed, We have given the Scripture to the family of Abraham and the kingdom, and We have given them a great kingdom." Allah says: do they envy people for the bounty He has given them? Envy is a blameworthy trait, and the envier wishes the bounty to be removed from his brother. But Allah has given the Book to the family of Abraham and the kingdom, and given them a great kingdom, so the bounty is from Him, and He gives to whom He wills, and the envier harms only himself. The exegetes differed over whom Allah meant by the people: some said the Prophet in particular, others the believers, others the people of the Book. In any case, the bounty is the prophethood and the Book, given to the family of Abraham, and the envier wishes it removed from his brother, but the bounty remains, and Allah is All-Generous, and He gives to whom He wills, and the envier harms only himself, for Allah knows the envious and He will requite them. And He is All-Wise.

phrases.ar: فَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَآ ءَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُم مُّلۡكًا عَظِيمٗا
phrases.translation: the descendants of Abraham the Book and wisdom, along with great authority
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, We have given the Scripture to the family of Abraham and the kingdom, and We have given them a great kingdom." This is the bounty of Allah, given to the prophets from the family of Abraham, and the kingdom given to some of them, and it is a great bounty, so do not envy, for Allah gives whom He wills, and He is All-Knowing of who deserves it. And the kingdom given to the prophets, David and Solomon, was a great kingdom, and the Book was given to their offspring, so the bounty is great, and do not envy, for Allah is All-Knowing of who deserves the bounty, and He gives it to whom He wills, and He is All-Just, and He does not wrong anyone, and the believers should be content with what Allah has given them.
